data.title: Narrative Deployed Against a Breaking Incident
data.summary:
Campaign content was published during an active incident involving the organisation,
exploiting the period before authoritative information was available.
data.description:
The information vacuum during an incident is the operation's opportunity. The
organisation cannot yet say what happened, the audience wants an explanation, and a
confident account — however unfounded — fills the space and becomes the reference point
against which the eventual official account is judged.

Speed of deployment is diagnostic. Content that is substantive and well-produced within
the first hours was prepared, which means either foreknowledge or a standing capability
aimed at the organisation. Both are significant findings and should be distinguished
carefully, since the first implies a much more serious compromise.

Incident response and communications are usually working separately at this point, which
is the condition the campaign exploits.
data.recommendation:
* Hold a pre-agreed holding statement that can be issued within minutes, so the vacuum is
  not left open.
* Connect incident response and communications from the first hour, under one decision
  owner.
* Assess whether prepared content implies foreknowledge, and treat that as a separate and
  more serious finding.
data.short_recommendation: Fill the vacuum with a pre-agreed holding statement in the first hour.
